subject: Hospitality
title: Rate Parity: The Controversial Rule
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Rate Parity: The Controversial Rule.

hook.text: Rate parity means a hotel must charge the same price everywhere—its website, Booking.com, Expedia. The same room, the same price.

buildup.text: OTAs demand rate parity in their contracts. They argue it's unfair if hotels undercut them on their own websites.

discovery.text: Many hotels hate rate parity because they can't offer direct booking discounts without violating OTA agreements.

twist.text: Europe banned rate parity in several countries. Hotels there can now offer cheaper direct rates, shifting power back from OTAs.

climax.text: The battle over rate parity is really about who controls pricing. Hotels want freedom; OTAs want a level playing field.

punchline.text: Same price everywhere—or not. Rate parity is a power struggle.

quiz.question: What is rate parity?
options: A rule requiring hotels to charge the same price across all booking channels
Equal room sizes across all floors
